messages.content: Can you fetch the server's response if I send a GET request to 'https://api.intent.com/query' with the following queries to recognize their corresponding intents: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there]? The list of intent-codes is [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye].

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the server's response. This is typically used for API calls and web content fetching. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. Must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS endpoint, such as 'https://api.example.com/data'.

intents.description: A list of intent codes derived from user queries, represented as strings. For example, ['weather', 'news'].

timeout.description: The maximum time, in seconds, to wait for the server's response before the request times out. For example, a timeout of 30.0 seconds. This is a float type value.

User-Agent.description: The User-Agent header's value representing the client software identity, such as 'MyApp/1.0'.

Accept.description: The Accept header's value indicating the media types which are acceptable for the response, like 'application/json'.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to include in the request. If not provided, default headers will be used.

The user wants to fetch server's response by sending a GET request to 'https://api.intent.com/query' with queries: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there] and list of intent-codes: [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye].

We need to use the get_response function. Provide the URL, intents list, maybe queries? The function signature: get_response takes url, intents (list of intent codes), timeout, headers. It doesn't accept queries directly. But maybe we can pass queries as part of the URL? The user didn't specify how to send queries. Possibly we need to encode them as query parameters. But the function signature only includes url, intents, timeout, headers. So we can only pass intents. But the user wants to fetch server's response for those queries. We might need to construct the URL with query parameters. For example: https://api.intent.com/query?queries=hello,I want to transfer funds,show my balance,hey there&intents=get_balance,transfer_funds,hello,goodbye. But the function signature doesn't allow passing queries. But we can embed them in the URL string.

Thus we can call get_response with url: 'https://api.intent.com/query?queries=hello,I%20want%20to%20transfer%20funds,show%20my%20balance,hey%20there&intents=get_balance,transfer_funds,hello,goodbye'.

We also need to provide intents list? The function expects intents: string[]. We can pass the list. But the URL already includes intents. Might be redundant. But we can pass intents list as well.

{
